edges.description: Osteolytic resorption of the terminal phalangeal bone in the fingers directly produces radiographic acro-osteolysis of the distal hand phalanges.
Osteolytic resorption of the pedal terminal phalanges directly produces acro-osteolysis of the distal toe phalanges.
Progressive loss of distal phalangeal bone length directly causes visible shortening of affected fingers and toes.
Nail dystrophy over affected digits may reflect loss of the distal phalangeal bony support beneath the nail bed; the reported cases document co-occurrence rather than a demonstrated mechanism.
Distal interphalangeal flexion contractures occur in digits affected by advanced distal phalangeal osteolysis; the intervening steps are not established.
